records.name: GREAT (Germantown Residents for Economic Alternatives Together)
records.summary: A Germantown neighborhood group that shares seeds and tools, runs a mutual aid fund and time bank, and works on housing and emergency preparedness so current residents can stay.
records.what_you_do: Get on the email list, attend learning circles and events, and take part in projects such as the seed library, canning club, and housing outreach. Volunteers can also fill in the volunteer form on the site.

schedule.text: No regular meeting time is published. Learning circles run as short series of about 3 to 5 meetings, and events are posted on the events page.

first_step.how: Join the email list on the website, then attend an event you hear about, or fill in the volunteer form on the Get involved page.
first_step.basis: The email list, the volunteer form and the event register links are all public, and the site suggests attending an event as a first step. No event times or places are posted and no membership step is shown, so the rating stays at 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: The events page and newsletter are where activity is posted, and the site does not say how long events run, who attends, or what they cost. The group says many members first came through a learning circle, an event, or volunteering. Email greatgtown@gmail.com to ask about the next event before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email for the time and place of the next event, since the events page does not show them.
The group's address is a post office box, so the meeting place will come from the event notice or the reply to your email.
Follow the group on Facebook or Instagram, where event posts go up.

records.notes: Status moved from probably_active to dormant because the newest dated item on the events archive is an August 2024 newsletter notice, which is more than 24 months old. The Germantown Visioning and Collective Action Assembly is listed as upcoming with a register link but no date, so a reviewer may want to confirm activity with the group before publishing. The learning circle sign-up page names an individual organizer's personal email address; we did not record it and used the group's address instead. The 2025 copyright footer was not counted as evidence.

records.name: Good As Gold Foundation
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches money skills and homebuying readiness through workshops and a nine-month cohort, and gives grants to families facing hardship.
records.what_you_do: Attend a financial workshop, apply to the Golden Keys homebuying cohort, or join the email list. Volunteers can fill in the volunteer interest form, and partners and speakers have their own sign-up pages.

schedule.text: Golden Keys is a nine-month cohort of 13 to 16 sessions, each 1 to 2 hours, offered virtually and in person. Golden Workshops run in person or online, as single events or as a series.

first_step.how: Use the Apply Here form on the Golden Keys page to apply for the homebuying cohort, or attend a Golden Workshop listed on the events page.
first_step.basis: The events page lists a public interest meeting before the cohort application, and workshops link to sign up on the events page. The cohort needs an application and holds 25 people, and the site does not say who may attend workshops, so the rating is 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Golden Workshops cover money topics such as budgeting, taxes, credit, and homeownership, in person or online. The Golden Keys cohort meets in 13 to 16 sessions of 1 to 2 hours over about nine months, with budgeting, credit education, savings guidance, and one-on-one counseling. The site does not say what either one costs, so ask before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Email programs@goodasgoldfoundation.org about cost, eligibility, and location before you apply.
Choose in person or virtual when you sign up, since the cohort and the workshops are offered both ways.
Watch the events page for the interest meeting, which lets you learn about the cohort before you apply.

records.notes: The summary is corrected: the grants are large (the home page reports $15,000 each to 26 families), so the earlier words 'small grants' were removed. No cost or eligibility is published for workshops or the cohort. Two IRS mailing addresses are kept from tier 1; only the 441 E High Street office is confirmed on the contact page. Golden Keys is a 2026 to 2027 cohort, so its dates are kept out of the schedule text.

records.name: Here to Help Resource Center
records.summary: A help center for neighbors who need a hand with basic needs. It offers food, clothing, back-to-school supplies, help applying for grants and aid, job search support, and referrals to other services.
records.what_you_do: Ask for help with food, clothing, school supplies, aid applications, shelter, or job searching by phone, email, or the contact form. Volunteers and people joining programs use the Get involved page to apply.

schedule.text: Office hours are Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm, Friday and Saturday 9 am to 3 pm, and closed on Sunday.

first_step.how: Call +1 267-344-8376 during office hours, or send the contact form on the Contact page and choose Use Program, Volunteer, or Donate.
first_step.basis: Phone, email, a contact form and weekday hours are all listed on the contact page, so the way in is clear. Volunteers and people joining programs fill in an application first, so this is not rated 4.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tell the staff which help you need: food, clothing, school supplies, an aid application, or job search support. The site does not say what paperwork a service needs, how long it takes, or whether children can come without an adult, so ask those questions when you call.
first_visit_tips: Call during the posted hours, which end at 3 pm on Fridays and Saturdays and at 4 pm on other weekdays.
If you want to volunteer or join a program, have photo ID, emergency contact details, and a signed background check authorization ready, since the application lists them.
Sunday is closed, so plan around the weekday hours.

records.notes: Contact details, weekday hours and the application steps come from the group's own pages. The Sign Up and Donate buttons on the home page have no working link, and the daily workshops mentioned there have no times, so they are not recorded. The site gives no street address, cost, language or accessibility details; 5647 Heiskell St is the IRS mailing address. Tier 1 had two copies of that address, now merged. The background check is listed for volunteers and program applicants, and is not marked for people who only ask for help. The newcomer rating moved from 2 to 3 because the phone, email and form are now listed.

records.name: Incarnation Institute for Sex and Faith
records.summary: Teaches people about sex from a faith point of view, through webinars, resource sheets, and training for certified sex and faith educators.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a webinar or event from the Events page, or buy or read the resource sheets and discussion guides from the store. Professionals can apply to the educator training, which costs about $800 to $850. The site lists volunteer pages, but they describe no roles.

schedule.text: Webinars and events are listed on the Events page with a sign up button. Educator training is a multi-week course with weekly readings, videos, and assigned projects.

cost.text: Educator training costs about $800 to $850, with a $50 application deposit. Webinar and event prices are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Click To Sign Up button on the Events page to join a webinar or event. For the educator training, complete the online application form, then email two references and your essay to admin@incarnationinstitute.org.
first_step.basis: Events have a public sign up button and no application is shown for them. The educator training needs an application, two references, an essay, a deposit and a phone interview, so it is not a walk in.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Events page shows only a season, not a day, time, or format. The educator training is a course of weekly readings, videos, and assigned projects, with preparation due before each session. Accepted applicants have a phone interview.
first_visit_tips: Check the day, time, and format on the sign up page before you register, since the Events page shows only a season.
For the educator training, prepare two references and a 300 to 500 word essay before you apply.
The site says the group does not turn away people who cannot pay, so ask about financial help before you decide.

records.notes: The Events page lists only 'Spring 2026' for its latest event, with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out and the active status rests on that 2026 listing. The training fee and application details come from a page showing February 2025 dates, so the fee may be out of date. The site does not say who events are for, and it publishes no phone number or volunteer role description. The home page calls the organization a sex-positive Christian group; the audience faith field is left out because no tradition is named beyond that.

records.name: Bhakti Recovery Group
records.summary: A 12-step recovery fellowship for people working on addiction and related struggles. It adds bhakti yoga, a devotional practice, to the steps, and the only membership requirement is a wish to recover.
records.what_you_do: Join one of the about 20 Zoom meetings on the Meetings page, most of them open to anyone. Most meetings draw on Bhakti texts such as the Bhagavad Gita or Prabhupada's writings. Men's meetings are closed to others, and the one in-person meeting listed is in Mayapur, India.

schedule.text: The Meetings page lists about 20 Zoom meetings by day of the week, with times mostly in Eastern time and a few in other time zones. Several are men's meetings only. Times are as posted on the group's site.

cost.text: No meeting fee is listed. The site has donation and support pages.

first_step.how: Open the Meetings page on bhaktirecoverygroup.com, pick an open meeting that fits your time zone, and join it on Zoom with the link listed there.
first_step.basis: Open meetings are listed with a join link, and the site says the only requirement is wanting recovery. The pages read do not say newcomers are welcomed by name, so the rating is 3.
first_step.what_to_expect: Meetings follow the 12 steps, and most draw on Bhakti texts such as the Bhagavad Gita or Prabhupada's writings, so expect a spiritual element. The listed times show when each meeting starts and ends, but the pages do not say whether you will be asked to speak.
first_visit_tips: Convert the Eastern time to your own time zone before you join, since most listings use Eastern time.
Join a few minutes early to check your audio and video, since meetings are on Zoom.
Pick an open meeting; men's meetings are for men only.

records.notes: Meeting list (20 Zoom meetings and one in-person meeting) read from the group's own pages on 2026-10-08. Judgment call for the reviewer: the only in-person meeting is in Mayapur, India, and the Philadelphia address comes from the IRS record only. The meetings are online and open to anyone, so publish is proposed, but out_of_area is the alternative. One Monday listing reads 11:00 to 12:00 'am' and is probably a typo; it is not used in the schedule text. The event list shows a January 2027 Discovery Group event and an October retreat with no year, so neither is recorded as dated evidence. Meeting links and passcodes are left out. The IRS address is recorded as a mailing address, not as a meeting place.

records.name: Let Me Breathe
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works with area youth and police, gives a training scholarship called the Life Award, and supports seniors, people in prison, military families, and young children who have lost both parents.
records.what_you_do: Email the group to ask about its youth, senior, and outreach work, or about the Life Award training scholarship. Donations can be sent by email or PayPal.

cost.text: The site lists no program fees and does not say which programs are free.

first_step.how: Email letmebreatheinc@gmail.com and ask how to get involved, or ask about the Life Award training scholarship.
first_step.basis: Email is the only route on the site. No program schedule, application form, eligibility rules, or meeting place is listed, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a visit, a program session, a meeting place, or how often anything happens. Your first contact is an email, and the reply will set the next steps.
first_visit_tips: In your first email, say which program you are asking about, such as youth, seniors, or the Life Award.
Ask about cost, eligibility, and where the program happens, since the site lists none of these.

records.notes: Thin record. The site has no program pages: /about and /contact returned HTTP 404, and the home page links only to an email address and photos. One web search found no independent source for the group or the Life Award scholarship; its one hit for Cynthia Reed was a different person and was not used. Philadelphia appears on the site only as the founder's home, so the city link rests on the IRS record. Publish is proposed because the group takes requests by email; the reviewer may prefer to hold it until the group answers an inquiry. The home page names the founder as Cynthia Johnson-Reed, while the IRS record reads Cynthia J Reed; the tier 1 name is kept.

records.name: Mauckingbird Theatre Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia theatre company that stages affordable plays with LGBTQ themes. The site lists A Midsummer Night's Dream, presented with Hedgerow Theatre, as its current show, and actors audition for each show when a call is posted.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to the current show through the ticket link on the homepage, or watch the Opportunities page for an actor call for a specific production.

schedule.text: Productions run for set dates, and actor calls are posted for specific shows only.

cost.text: Tickets are sold online through the ticket link on the homepage. The pages read did not show prices.

first_step.how: Buy tickets to the current production through the Tickets link on the homepage, or watch the Opportunities page for an open call for a specific show.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public with online tickets. Actor submissions are taken only for specific shows when a call is posted, so acting depends on the next call.
first_step.what_to_expect: The current show is staged at Hedgerow Theatre in Rose Valley, outside Philadelphia, so plan the trip. The pages read did not give performance dates, times, or prices, so check the ticket page before you travel. If an audition call is posted, the notice sets out how to apply.
first_visit_tips: Check the ticket page for dates and times before you travel, since the company's own pages did not show them.
Plan travel for Rose Valley, which is outside the city.
The company's Facebook and Instagram pages are linked from the homepage, so follow them for updates.

records.notes: Status moved from probably_active to dormant under the dating rule: the newest dated item the site shows is the August 2016 production run on the Opportunities page. The homepage copyright year is not counted. The current show is listed without dates, so a reviewer may want to confirm activity before publishing. The current show's venue is in Rose Valley, outside the city. The mailing address 8708 Prospect Ave Apt B6 reads like an apartment, so the owner may want to confirm it is a business address before it stays published. The Hedgerow Theatre production page returned HTTP 404 and was not used.
